title: Carrollian axion electrodynamics
abstract: We construct theories of Carrollian electromagnetism coupled to an axion field. Obtained by performing a $c \to 0$ expansion of axion electrodynamics, these are of two types: electric and magnetic. We derive the Lagrangians and work out the general classical solutions for both. While the electric theory has the axion effectively decoupled from the electromagnetic fields, the magnetic theory is endowed with a nontrivial axion coupling that leads to interesting phenomenology. In particular, a Carrollian analogue of the Witten effect, wherein a magnetic monopole in the presence of a constant non-vanishing axion acquires an electric charge and becomes a dyon, is present in the magnetic theory. At the same time, the linear magnetoelectric effect vanishes entirely, a conclusion we establish by performing a thorough Dirac-Bergmann analysis of the constraint structure of the magnetic theory and a proper identification of its physical phase space.
summary: This work develops the effective field theory describing axion electrodynamics in the low-velocity (Carrollian) limit. It derives two distinct theories, highlighting that the magnetic sector supports a novel monopole-to-dyon conversion effect. The analysis rigorously proves the vanishing of the linear magnetoelectric effect while establishing the complex structure of the resulting phase space.
main_problem: The paper constructs and analyzes theories of Carrollian electromagnetism coupled to an axion field by performing a low-energy limit expansion ($c 	o 0$) of full axion electrodynamics.
main_result: The resulting magnetic theory exhibits a Carrollian analogue of the Witten effect, and the linear magnetoelectric effect is shown to vanish entirely through rigorous constraint analysis.
method: The primary method involves performing a systematic $c 	o 0$ expansion of the Lagrangian density and subsequently employing Dirac-Bergmann analysis to determine the physical phase space structure.
model_or_system: The system is axion electrodynamics, which is reduced to two types of Carrollian theories (electric and magnetic) in the low-velocity limit. The analysis extends to include couplings to fermions and non-Abelian generalizations.
key_observables: Carrollian analogue of the Witten effect (monopole acquiring electric charge), vanishing linear magnetoelectric effect, and non-vanishing Dirac brackets among canonical variables.
important_parameters: The speed of light ($c$), the axion mass ($m$), and the coupling constant ($\alpha$) are central parameters defining the limits and couplings.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies fundamentally on the $c 	o 0$ expansion methodology, and the initial Lagrangian is assumed to be the standard axion electrodynamics form.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from deriving the general $c 	o 0$ expansion for the Lagrangian, separating it into electric and magnetic theories, establishing key physical consequences like the Witten effect, and concluding with detailed analyses of the phase space structure using Dirac brackets.
why_interesting: The study of effective field theories in extreme limits (like $c 	o 0$) and the resulting topological phenomena (like the Witten effect) provides a framework for understanding low-energy effective theories in condensed matter systems, particularly those involving emergent gauge fields or topological order.
